benchmark_kind: commissioning and turnover readiness, evidence-chain closure, punch/NCR and dossier cases plus project-package cases
reference: Hand-built commissioning and turnover states in the tool-neutral vocabulary of SPEC-commissioningturnover.md section 13.1 (v2, read 2026-09-22): the four v2 presets P-A..P-D of section 9 with their stated expectations, the eight-link evidence chain (System/Package -> Requirement -> Test/Inspection -> Evidence -> Punch/NCR -> Closure -> Turnover dossier -> Accepted) with every link as the first broken one, chain_enforce yes against no on the same state, the punch/NCR register (categories A/B/C, NCR dispositions use-as-is / repair / rework / reject, concession links, closure records, transfer agreements, void items, ages and mean closure duration), dossier index assembly and completeness, acceptance recording, every flag kind of section 4.8, and the retained v1 rule corpus (applicability, gate status, prerequisite edges, exceptions, conditions, dependencies, test packages, gaps and the frontier). Every reference value was computed by commissioningturnover-ref.py, an independent standard-library re-implementation of spec sections 3-6 written without access to the tool code, and each value is also stated by hand in that script's case builders; a disagreement between the two aborts the build. Test-phase vocabulary follows IEC 62381:2024 (FAT 3.1.8, SAT 3.1.19, SIT 3.1.20, punch list 3.1.16), the loop-check position follows IEC 62382:2024 cl. 1.1, the transition and verification process names follow ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 6.4.9-6.4.11, the acceptance, systems-manual and training documents follow ASHRAE Guideline 0-2019 cl. 7-8 and App. H/M/O/P, and rework/repair follow ISO 9000:2015 3.12.8/3.12.9; the categories, the chain, the dossier completeness rules and every severity are the spec's author method.
provenance_note: The 46 recorded cases keep their expected values beside the rule engine and detect a change in a graded outcome without establishing that the outcome was right to begin with. The 121 corpus cases were authored from the public specification without access to this code and are recomputed here.
tolerance: Categorical comparison of readiness, rule ids, chain link status, dossier index contents and save outcome; punch ages and the mean closure time are whole-day integers compared exactly (the mean to 0.1 d), across 964 graded comparisons.

manifest.note: Manifest v2 parsed; seven languages in catalog_languages and tool_languages; project_package declares four written paths.

rule_corpus.note: Every dependency edge and item policy references an existing evidence item.

v1_regression.note: The 24 recorded rule cases and the 11 recorded package cases run unchanged in meaning; their inputs carry chain_enforce "no" and the package cases assert the v2 declaration.

adapter.note: Corpus cases are mapped onto the state of SPEC §3.2 and evaluated with solve(), assembleIndex() and pkgIdProblems(), the functions the interface uses.

browser_framework.note: Framework browser, PDF and mobile checks are recorded in the delivery note, not in this artifact.

not_benchmarked: COM-R-068 MODEL_INTEGRITY: a self-check over the rule corpus ('an edge or policy names a missing item'). No input state can trigger it, so the corpus only asserts its absence.

Package transport (spec 7.1): the explicit Load, the section mapping, the replaced/unmapped/ignored report, the digest and the conflict rule. Cases hand the `imported` projection directly, as section 13.1 allows; package cases belong to TZ-project-package 7 QA.

Written register shapes (spec 7.3) and the saved `turnover_dossiers[].chain` block: the corpus grades the save outcome (ok / refused, and whether a name is listed as offending) but not the written field values.

The 'Convert punch conditions to the punch register' action (spec 10, panel 6), 'Assemble index' as an interactive action and the permalink: actions and UI state, not expressible in the 13.1 input vocabulary. Assembly itself is graded through the assembled index of each case.
Rendering, layout, mobile behaviour, figures, report pagination, the seven languages and the Python export decline (spec 14).
Messages, next actions and basis strings of findings: only rule id, legacy id, system, severity, gate and chain link are graded (spec 13.2).

Whether the punch categories, the eight links, the dossier sections and the severities are the right engineering choice: author method (spec 14). Nothing here demonstrates conformity with any cited standard.
Contents of referenced documents, test sheets or certificates - the tool never reads them (spec 2.3).

Sibling vocabularies beyond the field names of spec 3.5 (deviation status words, functional-test result words, vendor-document status/maturity words): the corpus uses the values the spec lists; a mismatch with a sibling tool is an integration issue for the coordinator (spec 14 and the spec's open questions 1-3).

With two dossiers for one system (COM-R-161) the rules read the first row in state order (spec changelog 2026-09-23); COM-R-101 and the save outcome are graded, COM-R-162..177 are not, because the second row of that case is empty and grading them would only restate the first row.

Whether a flag whose target_kind is outside the runtime FLAG_KINDS list of diagram-project.js is additionally reported as COM-R-182: the spec requires the reopening (4.8, acceptance 5). punch_item is in fact listed by the runtime, so the case flags-reopen-l2-l4-l6-l7 simply does not assert that absence.
Which fields a test-derived evidence record carries beyond status and reference (spec 4.4 names only those two), so no case makes COM-R-057 or COM-R-058 depend on a derived criterion or owner.

The `system` field of a project-level finding (COM-R-048, COM-R-170): the spec changelog of 2026-09-23 settles it on the v1 behaviour frozen by acceptance criterion 1, and 13.2 does not grade that field.
